items.facts: Deloitte released its State of AI in the Enterprise report on October 29, based on a survey of 3,500 director to C-suite leaders across 25 countries and six industries, conducted in May and June 2026. It found 81% report faster decision-making and execution, while 28% report revenue gains from AI, up from 20% in January, and only 25% say they are using AI to deeply transform the business.
items.headline: Deloitte: AI speeds decisions, but deeper change lags
items.relevance: The gap between speed and deeper change means redesigned roles and decision rights matter as much as the tools themselves.

sources.title: Deloitte, Enterprise AI enters an ROI reckoning

items.facts: Randstad released its 2026 tech talent report on October 29, combining survey data from 1,100 senior business and technology decision-makers across 11 markets with labor data covering more than 20 million job postings. It found 93% of US organizations are increasing tech headcount, System Architecture and AI Orchestration is the hardest capability to recruit at 41%, and US entry-level generative AI developers start at $152,000, 12.6% higher than traditional senior developers at $135,000.
items.headline: 93% of US employers are growing tech headcount
items.relevance: Hiring plans now compete hardest for orchestration skills and higher entry-level pay, since those are the scarcest parts of the market.

sources.title: Randstad via PR Newswire, AI adoption accelerates talent demand

items.facts: Insperity and Lighthouse Research and Advisory released The AI Balance Gap on October 29, based on surveys completed in the second quarter of 2026 by 800 full-time US workers and 1,037 leaders at small and medium businesses. Organizations that invest as intentionally in people as in technology report approximately 2x stronger results across five workforce and leadership measures, yet only four in 10 leaders feel very prepared to manage the people side of AI change while 75% are actively using or experimenting with AI.
items.headline: Firms balancing AI and people report stronger results
items.relevance: Training, communication, and change plans alongside tool rollouts are what separate stronger results from faster tools alone.

sources.title: Insperity via Business Wire, SMBs that balance AI and people investment

items.facts: Adobe published its September 2026 US retail AI traffic findings on October 29, based on more than 1 trillion visits to US retail sites, 100 million products, and 18 product categories. AI-referred traffic converted 90% better than non-AI traffic and generated 83% higher revenue per visit, while AI traffic to US retail sites grew 71% year over year.
items.headline: AI-referred shoppers convert 90% better, Adobe finds
items.relevance: That traffic now arrives further along in buying, so how a team's pages read to AI systems affects which shoppers it reaches.

sources.title: Search Engine Land, AI traffic drives more revenue per visit
